business_problem: A global biopharmaceutical company had already begun using AI but lacked a mature governance model, creating gaps in how projects were reviewed for bias, privacy, third-party risk and regulatory readiness at a time when AI-specific regulation was quickly emerging.
solution_summary: EY used its global Responsible AI framework to evaluate and strengthen the biopharma company's AI-governance operating model. The engagement started with the client's own draft governance framework and responsible-AI principles, then overlaid EY's methodology through interviews, documentation reviews and project-level assessments. Multidisciplinary teams of digital ethicists, IT-risk practitioners, data scientists and subject-matter experts examined how AI risks were handled across the lifecycle-from problem identification through modeling, deployment and monitoring-and reviewed live projects such as forecasting, adverse-event tracking and early disease detection. The review exposed gaps in project-level controls and led to recommended changes including stronger third-party AI assessment and creation of a central AI inventory. The result was a more operational compliance structure the company could use to align teams and prepare for expanding regulation.

solution_components.name: global Responsible AI framework
solution_components.role: Provides the review methodology EY used to evaluate governance, controls and lifecycle risk management.

solution_components.name: AI governance framework
solution_components.role: Defines the client's principles, accountabilities and minimum requirements for AI use.

solution_components.name: central AI inventory
solution_components.role: Creates a foundational registry of AI systems needed for risk management and regulatory compliance.

solution_components.name: third-party AI risk assessment
solution_components.role: Strengthens oversight of vendor and external AI risks that were previously under-addressed.

data_flow: AI projects and supporting documentation are reviewed against the global Responsible AI framework, with findings feeding changes to the client's governance framework, project requirements and inventory controls. That governance loop then applies back to AI systems under development, deployment and monitoring across the organization.
business_outcome: The biopharma company gained a more operational AI-governance model with clearer minimum requirements, stronger third-party oversight and better readiness for regulatory scrutiny, reducing the risk that AI projects would drift away from stated ethical principles.
architecture_clues: EY reviewed both the governance framework and a sample of live AI projects.
The framework is meant to work across a federated organization rather than a single centralized AI team.
A central AI inventory was identified as foundational to ongoing risk management.
Third-party AI review was one of the concrete control gaps the assessment surfaced.
